description: Strongest by far when one side has an open three on the bottom row (three in a row with both end cells empty, so two playable winning cells on row 0); activation is then 10-21. Weaker firing near threshold comes from other immediate threats: any single winning/blocking cell on the bottom row, or an opponent must-block (often a vertical three) in columns 2-3. Most threat positions outside these do not fire; elevated (row 1+) open threes do not.
effect: Mostly none measurable (fires in decided positions). When two bottom-row winning moves exist, forcing it high shifts about 0.2 probability toward the left winning cell (e.g. col 5 to col 2).
notes: 7 score calls. Bottom-row open three alone: precision ~.5 but recall .09. Any threat: recall .77 precision .13. Best p6 (bottom-row playable win cell either side, or must-block above row 0 in cols 2-3): F1 0.365, P .28, R .53, AUROC .74, simulation share 0.15. Minimal pairs: bottom-row double threat is robust (15-21); near-threshold behaviour depends on unrelated stones and is left/right asymmetric, looks like a mixture. Synthesis 4,4,5,4,3,0 = 21.72 beats dev max.
